body:
Fixes #2202.

## The problem, stated precisely

A provider ships a model on a Tuesday. Hive Mind cannot name it until the next release.

`src/models/index.mjs` was a static table, and `--model` validated against nothing else — so "support for new models" was, structurally, a release-cadence problem wearing a catalogue's clothes. The issue asks for the catalogue to stop being a snapshot, with one hard constraint attached:

> models extraction should never trigger any tokens expense, otherwise such methods must be excluded from our codebase

That constraint is what makes this more than an HTTP fetch, and it is the reason the design below puts the guarantee in the source table rather than in each caller.

## What this changes

### The models themselves (R1)

Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Cyber, with aliases, context windows, capability sets and fallback chains. The additions pushed `src/models/index.mjs` past the 1350-line early warning in `scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`, so the catalogue itself moved to a new leaf module `src/models/catalog.mjs` and is re-exported — **the public surface is unchanged**, which the existing model tests prove by still passing untouched.

### The catalogue hot-loads (R2, R7, R8, R9)

Four modules, split on the seam that already existed:

| Module | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `src/model-catalogue-sources.lib.mjs` | the source table, both token-free guards, the rejected-methods record |
| `src/model-catalogue-fetch.lib.mjs` | one reader per source, each normalising a different response shape |
| `src/model-catalogue.lib.mjs` | the TTL cache, the merge, the router lease |
| `src/model-catalogue-render.lib.mjs` | pure formatting — testable with no I/O at all |

Six sources, merged in a fixed precedence:

| # | Source | Contributes | Why here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Link.Assistant Router | availability | the only source that can say a model is reachable *through the path a routed task will take* |
| 2 | `codex debug models` | availability | the installed binary's own catalogue, no network call |
| 3 | Anthropic `GET /v1/models` | availability | what this key is entitled to |
| 4 | OpenAI `GET /v1/models` | availability | same shape, same reasoning |
| 5 | models.dev | **metadata only** | context, pricing, modality, release date — it never adds a model to the available list, because it knows nothing about this account |
| 6 | Bundled | availability | `src/models/catalog.mjs`: the offline floor and the spelling authority |

Answers are cached per source and per tool for **at least** an hour. `HIVE_MIND_MODEL_CATALOGUE_TTL_MINUTES` can only *raise* that floor — a lower value would ask providers more often, which is the thing R9 exists to prevent. A failed source never poisons the cache: the last good answer is reused, marked stale, and the failure is printed.

### Listing models cannot cost a token — structurally (R7)

Two deliberately redundant guards, both in the module where a source is *declared*, so the property cannot be lost at a call site:

- **`assertTokenFreeSource`** rejects any descriptor that has not explicitly declared `billable: false`. A source cannot become billable by omission; the table is checked at module load.
- **`assertTokenFreeUrl`** rejects any URL whose path is terminal-billable — `/v1/messages`, `/chat/completions`, `:generateContent`, … — whatever descriptor carried it. A typo turning `/v1/models` into `/v1/messages` **throws instead of spending**.

The other half of R7 is the record of what was *not* implemented, so "we don't do that" is reviewable rather than merely absent:

| Rejected | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Drive the Claude Code TUI `/model` picker | starting the TUI starts a session, and Claude Code sends a request at session start — the cost is real, invisible, and lands on someone else's bill |
| Drive the Codex TUI `/model` picker | `codex debug models` returns the same catalogue as JSON with no network call, so the TUI buys only cost and flakiness |
| Probe a completion endpoint for an id | one token is still a billed request, and a 404 for an unknown model is indistinguishable from a 404 for an unentitled one |
| Scrape vendor docs HTML | free but unversioned and layout-dependent; models.dev is the same data behind a stable contract |

### `/models` and `hive-models` (R5)

Three groups, which is exactly the "fully supported → hot loaded" spectrum the issue asks to see:

```
Models for claude (default: opus)
3 bundled and live · 2 hot loaded · 14 bundled only

Bundled and live (3) — shipped with this installation and confirmed reachable now
  * claude-opus-5 (opus, opus-5) [1M ctx · 128K out · $5/$25 per Mtok · reasoning · text+image+pdf · 2026-07-24]
Hot loaded (2) — a live source has them, this installation does not ship them
Bundled only (14) — shipped, but no live source confirmed them

Sources, in the order they are trusted:
  - Link.Assistant Router: ok — 41 model(s)
  - Anthropic GET /v1/models: skipped — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set
  - models.dev: ok — specifications for 3570 model(s)
Live answers are cached for 1h 0m; pass --refresh to ignore the cache.
```

The footer names every source actually consulted and its outcome, so *"why don't I see X"* is answerable from the output alone. Flags: `--tool` (repeatable), `--details`, `--refresh`, `--json`, and `--all` in Telegram. In chat the same flags are accepted the way a chat writes them — `/models codex`, `/models --tool codex` and `/models --tool=codex` are one command, because a chat is not a shell.

With `HIVE_MIND_MODELS_HOT_LOAD=0` the third heading is just **Bundled** — calling those models "unconfirmed" when no live source was consulted would be an accusation the command cannot support.

### `--use-router` speaks both route dialects (R3, R4)

Measured, not assumed. Both images were started **exactly the way Hive Mind starts them** and every path probed from inside the container:

| Path | `0.119.0` | `1.2.0` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/health` | **200** | 404 |
| `/api/health` | 404 | **200** |
| `/v1/models` | **401** | 404 |
| `/api/services/anthropic/v1/models` | 404 | **401** |
| `/api/v3/rate_limit` (what `gh` emits) | **401** | 404 |
| `/api/services/github/api/v3/rate_limit` | 404 | **401** |

The dialects are **disjoint** — there is no overlap column — so migrating the URLs and moving the pin are one atomic change, not two. `src/router-routes.lib.mjs` derives every base URL, the health probe and the catalogue path from the pinned image, so the pin can move in one line when it is safe to.

It is **not** safe yet, and that is the one requirement this repository cannot fully satisfy on its own: router `1.x` serves GitHub under `/api/services/github/api/…`, `gh` builds a custom host's REST base as `https://<host>/api/v3/`, and `gh` exposes no path-prefix option. So the pin moves to `0.125.4` (the highest `0.x`) rather than to `1.x`, nothing #2164 shipped is lost, and choosing `1.x` via `HIVE_MIND_ROUTER_IMAGE` is an informed trade reported by `describeRouterCoverageGaps` instead of discovered at runtime.

Per the issue's own instruction to report missing features upstream, three issues were filed: [router#415](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/415) (no `gh`-reachable REST base — the blocker), [router#417](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/417) (one merged catalogue route instead of five service-specific ones), [router#418](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/418) (catalogue metadata beyond the id).

Credential adoption — the "mounted with claude and codex credential files/folders" half of R3 — already works; it is measured and quoted in the case study rather than reimplemented.

### A stale CLI is refreshed before the run needs it (R6)

An outdated `claude` or `codex` binary is the usual reason a brand-new model name is rejected, so every command that drives one checks first: `/solve`, `/hive`, `/task`, `/fix`, `/models`, `hive-models`.

The check is deliberately timid — throttled to once per 6 hours, narrowed to the one CLI in play, deferred entirely while other tasks run, skipped for `--dry-run` / `--only-prepare-command`, and never fatal.

**The load-bearing detail:** the idle gate finds busy tasks by scanning process command lines for issue URLs, so a `/solve` asking for an update would find *itself* and defer forever. Every caller passes `ignoreTasks` with its own task reference — removing exactly one process, its own, and leaving every genuinely concurrent task blocking the swap. In a `/hive` fan-out of *N* children, each excludes only itself, sees the other *N*−1, and defers. That is correct: a CLI must never be replaced underneath a running task.

`/fix` needed no code change — `partitionFixArgs` already forwards flags into the `/solve` child it starts — but that is asserted end to end rather than assumed.

Opt out with `--no-tool-update` (accepted by every one of the six commands) or `HIVE_MIND_AGENTIC_CLI_AUTO_UPDATE=0`.

### The case study (R10)

`docs/case-studies/issue-2202/` — the issue and PR feeds, the pinned code state, the router's release history and route contract, six reproducible measurements, vendor-quoted specifications, a `MANIFEST.md` with a SHA-256 for every artifact, the requirement-by-requirement plan, and a final part recording what shipped **differently** from that plan and why.

## Tests

206 assertions across four new suites, all reproducing the gap before fixing it:

| Suite | Assertions | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/test-issue-2202-new-model-support.mjs` | 69 | R1 — the new ids, aliases, fallbacks, and that no existing alias regressed |
| `tests/test-issue-2202-router-routes.mjs` | 70 | R3/R4 — both dialects, every derived URL, the health probe, the coverage gaps |
| `tests/test-issue-2202-model-catalogue.mjs` | 32 | R2/R7/R8/R9 — the merge, the TTL floor, both token-free guards, stale reuse |
| `tests/test-issue-2202-models-command.mjs` | 35 | R5/R6 — parsing, rendering, the freshness wiring in all four commands |

Full suite: 451 files, green. `npm run lint`, `format:check`, `check-file-line-limits` and the docs sync tests all pass.

Two live smoke runs are quoted in `docs/MODELS.md` and the case study, including real models.dev specifications hot-loaded for `claude-fable-5-1`.

## Found by reviewing this diff, and fixed here

Four defects and one CodeQL alert, all written up in the case study:

- **A leased router token was quoted back at the operator.** `docker exec --env ROUTER_CATALOGUE_TOKEN=… ` fails with Node's `Command failed: <argv…>` message, and that message is what `/models` prints in its source footer. The failure is now described from stderr, the caught error is scrubbed before it is attached as a `cause`, and the regression test asserts the whole inspected error chain is clean — not just the top message.
- **The same hazard, two more command lines.** The router container is started with `--env TOKEN_SECRET=…` and its providers registered with `--api-key …`; both failure paths preferred stderr, which is empty when a process is killed on a timeout. `dockerErrorMessage` now masks `--env` values and `--api-key`/`--token`/`--secret`/`--password` arguments, and the four router call sites use it instead of repeating the expression.
- **`/task --dry-run` reached the registry.** A dry run drives no CLI, so it now installs nothing either — the same rule `/solve` already followed.
- **`--use-router` could leave a tool silently unrouted.** When the pinned dialect serves no endpoint for the tool (Gemini on the default legacy pin), no base URL is wired and the CLI calls the vendor directly with its own credential. The run now says so instead of looking routed.
- **CodeQL `js/clear-text-logging` (alert 259)** on a test that handed a `GEMINI_API_KEY`-named value to an assertion helper that prints what it compares. The comparison happens before the helper sees it now, matching the sibling issue-2164 suite.

## Documentation

`docs/MODELS.md` + `.zh` / `.hi` / `.ru`; `--tool-update` listed in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` in all four languages; the README's model section points at the new page in all four languages. Changeset added for a minor release.

## Deliberate non-goals

- **No default model changes.** Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra are more expensive than the current defaults and both are gated today. They become selectable, not automatic.
- **The bundled table is not replaced.** It is the offline floor and the spelling authority; the live catalogue annotates it.
- **Preview-gated models will not appear for most accounts.** By design — `/models` says so rather than pretending otherwise.
title: Hot-load the model catalogue, add /models, and stop shipping a stale model list
